name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=ani_decoder). Descriptor accurately reflects body: a frame-dispatch chunk handler (slot @ data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_frame_dispatch_table + 0x14 = 0x5277E, the sole DATA xref to this function; dispatch table @ 0x5276A entry index 5 = 0x36BB2 confirmed by reading the table dwords) that copies one full literal (raw, uncompressed) row of target_width bytes from the frame stream straight into the destination row buffer. 'row' distinguishes it from the palette-area sibling fd2_ani_decoder_chunk_palette_load_literal (which copies the 768-byte palette at src_buf); 'copy_literal' distinguishes it from row_fill_byte (broadcast one byte) and row_decode_rle (RLE-decoded). No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: ANI frame-decoder chunk handler (dispatch slot @ table+0x14): copy one full literal/raw destination row (data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_target_width bytes) verbatim from the frame stream into the destination buffer.
logic_summary: Loads EBX=target_width (ushort @ 0x52760) and EDI=dst_buf (@ 0x52762), copies width bytes from the ANI frame stream cursor (ESI) to the destination: REP MOVSD with ECX=width>>2 (width/4 dwords) followed by REP MOVSB with CL=(width&3) tail-remainder bytes. Equivalent to memcpy(dst_buf, stream, target_width). No return value; advances the stream cursor by target_width consumed bytes.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effect: writes target_width raw bytes copied from the frame stream into the destination row at data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_dst_buf; advances the frame-stream cursor (ESI in binary / g_ani_cursor in C) by target_width consumed bytes.

reads_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-scope static stream cursor; binary uses ESI register)
writes_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-scope static stream cursor; binary uses ESI register)
*data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_dst_buf (destination row buffer pointed to by dst_buf; the global pointer itself is only read)
notes: Source (anidec.c lines 178-186) is already a correct, concise C equivalent: width=target_width; memcpy(dst_buf, g_ani_cursor, width); g_ani_cursor += width. The binary's REP MOVSD (width/4 dwords) + REP MOVSB (width&3 bytes) == width-byte block copy == memcpy. Row-buffer analog of the palette sibling fd2_ani_decoder_chunk_palette_load_literal (0x36B01); same MOVSD/MOVSB literal-copy idiom but width/dst_buf-driven instead of fixed 768/src_buf. Source comment block (lines 173-177) is accurate and concise -> keep. Ghidra plate is far more detailed (register protocol ESI in/out, EBX/ECX/EDI clobbers, algorithm, dispatch slot 0x14 + caller chain: fd2_play_ani_file_animation_sequence -> fd2_ani_decoder_decode_frame_bytes @ 0x36C9E -> indirect via table @ 0x5276A -> here) and consistent with the source understanding -> not modified (ghidra_plate_action=none). Function is void(void) so params=[]. No normal CALL callers (get_function_callers empty); sole xref is the DATA pointer at 0x5277E in the dispatch table, consistent with the custom register-protocol indirect-call design. The binary's stream cursor is the ESI register handed off by the dispatcher; the C port models it via file-scope static g_ani_cursor. memcpy here is the canonical block-copy idiom and is the existing (already-verified) code; not a timing-sensitive scaling/blit hot loop, so no codegen-shape concern. Decompiler's '(byte)uVar1 & 0xffffff03' tail-loop count is just the AND BL,0x3 (width & 3) tail remainder, confirmed by disasm.
